name: Saw in Half
oracle_text: Destroy target creature. If that creature dies this way, its controller creates two tokens that are copies of that creature, except their power is half that creature's power and their toughness is half that creature's toughness. Round up each time.
blocked_sentences: Destroy target creature. If that creature dies this way, its controller creates two tokens that are copies of that creature, except their power is half that creature's power and their toughness is half that creature's toughness. Round up each time.

needs.what: copy_permanent's `except` power/toughness must accept a value expression evaluated at resolution (e.g. {"half": {"of": {"power_had": ...}, "round": "up"}} read from the destroyed creature's last known power/toughness), stored as the token's copiable base P/T
needs.why_existing_wont_do: copy_permanent's `except`/`except_` is a static dict copied verbatim into copy_overrides, and characteristics.py reads copy_overrides['power'/'toughness'] with int(), so only printed constants (eternalize's 4/4) work; the `half` value exists but cannot be fed into a copy exception

needs.what: a condition that the object destroyed by this spell's `destroy` (bound with `as`) actually died, i.e. went to the graveyard rather than being saved by indestructible/regeneration or replaced to exile, plus copy_permanent reaching that object in the graveyard and creating the tokens under its controller (controller: that creature's last controller)
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `destroy` has `as` and `if` has `zone_is`/`exists`, but no shipped card shows a 'dies this way' check on a destroyed target nor copy_permanent's controller resolving to the destroyed creature's last controller; low certainty this part is missing, the P/T exception is the definite blocker
